# Workflows

GitHub Actions workflows (C-0011 section 4). This README lives here and not in `.github/`, because GitHub would show a README in `.github/` on the repository's front page in place of the root README.

## ci.yml

Runs on every push and every pull request. The `ios` job runs for every pull request, on every push to one, and for every push to `main` (D7 in plan section 4.2), and so does the `runtime` job (D14). A push to another branch skips both, because the `pull_request` run of the same commit builds the merge result.

| Job | Runner | Steps |
|---|---|---|
| `dotnet` | `windows-2025` and `ubuntu-24.04` | Install the SDK that `global.json` pins and check it against the pin; restore NuGet's packages from the cache of `main`; restore `eng/ci.slnf` from the lock files, and fail if a lock file was written, because locked mode writes a missing one instead of failing; build it in Release; run its tests, with a skipped test counted as a failure; check its formatting and the formatting of the tools; publish the trimmed test app, which fails on any trimming warning; on a push to `main` only, save NuGet's packages to the cache. |
| `checks` | `ubuntu-24.04` | Install the SDK and the CI tools that `eng/toolchain.json` pins, each download checked against its SHA-256; check the SDK and the tools against their pins; run the tools' self-tests; then REUSE, gitleaks over the whole history (failing on a `.gitleaksignore`, which gitleaks would honor), the personal-data and forbidden-file check, lychee (online outside `docs/research/`, and offline for the relative links of the research notes), and the dependency licenses. |
| `native` | `xcode-27`, the image that `eng/toolchain.json` pins | Install the SDK that `global.json` pins; select the pinned Xcode with `eng/mac/select-xcode.sh`; run `eng/mac/bootstrap.sh --native`, which checks the SDK and Xcode, installs CMake and the LLVM release of clang-format and clang-tidy from their pinned downloads, checks them, and puts them on the PATH; print their versions; check the format of the native code with `eng/mac/check-native-style.sh`, and show that a planted format error in a scratch copy fails that check; build and run the CTest suite with the CMake presets `asan-ubsan` and `tsan`; run clang-tidy on the compile databases of `asan-ubsan`, `ios-device-test` and `ios-device`, the last two only configured; build the host test library with `macos-test`; restore, build and check the formatting of `tests/Paneport.Interop.Tests`, failing if a lock file was written; and run those tests against the library, with a skipped test counted as a failure. |
| `ios` | `xcode-27`, the image that `eng/toolchain.json` pins | Install the SDK that `global.json` pins; select the pinned Xcode with `eng/mac/select-xcode.sh`, through `DEVELOPER_DIR`, which refuses one that is a release candidate or a beta; run `eng/mac/bootstrap.sh --ios --forks`, which checks the SDK and Xcode against their pins, installs the iOS workload from the pinned workload set unless it is there, and CMake and the build tools of the forks from their pinned downloads, and checks them; run the bootstrap again, which must skip the workload's install and install no tool again; print the SDK, workload set, Xcode and CMake versions; run the bootstrap against another Xcode on the image, which must fail and name both versions; run `tools/CheckToolchain.cs -- --fork-tools` with Xcode's Python first on the PATH and without llvm-mingw, which must fail and name both; build `paneport_host.framework` with the CMake presets `ios-device` and `ios-device-test`, and check both with `eng/mac/check-framework.sh`; fetch the forks at depth 1 with the submodules of theirs that the first targets need, and run those targets: Wine's `configure` and build tools, its i386 libraries for DXMT, FEX's CMake configuration and DXMT's Meson setup of its 32-bit side ([forks.md](../../docs/design/forks.md) section 7); restore both flavors of the app, Paneport.iOS and the device test flavor of `tests/device`, from their lock files, and fail, printing the files, if a lock file was written; build both for `ios-arm64` in Release without signing, with the head commit and the run number for the build stamp and the job's switch for `extended-virtual-addressing`, which is off, and check their formatting; sign each ad hoc with `eng/mac/sign-adhoc.sh`, with no Apple identity; check each with `eng/mac/check-app.sh`; package each as an `.ipa` with `eng/mac/package-ipa.sh`; scan both with `tools/ScanPackage.cs`, each of these steps going on with the other flavor when one fails; then, only if every step before passed, upload them as `Paneport-main-<commit>` and `Paneport-test-<commit>` ([ios-app-head.md](../../docs/design/ios-app-head.md) section 11). |
| `runtime` | `xcode-27`, the image that `eng/toolchain.json` pins | Install the SDK that `global.json` pins; select the pinned Xcode with `eng/mac/select-xcode.sh`; compute the cache keys of C-0011 section 4; restore the build tools of the forks from the cache, run `eng/mac/bootstrap.sh --forks`, which installs what the cache did not bring and checks every tool against its pin, and save the tools unless they were restored; restore Wine's install and FEX's module from the cache, and build each one that is not there with `eng/mac/build-wine.sh` or `eng/mac/build-fex.sh`, after fetching its fork at depth 1, saving it to the cache right after the build; build the Win32 test programs of `tests/win32` with `eng/mac/build-win32-tests.sh x86_64`, with every warning an error, and analyze them with llvm-mingw's clang-tidy ([runtime-macos-harness.md](../../docs/design/runtime-macos-harness.md) section 8); build the harness with the CMake preset `macos-harness`; run the harness's cases with `eng/mac/run-harness.sh --mode multi`, which must pass, and its planted cases, which must fail and be named; upload the logs of the cases and of a fork build as `runtime-logs-<commit>-<attempt>`. |

- **Pins.** Actions are pinned to a full commit hash, with the release tag in a comment. Runner images are named by version, not `-latest`. The SDK comes from `global.json`, packages from the lock files, and the CI tools, Xcode, the iOS workload set, the macOS image, CMake, the LLVM release and the build tools of the forks from `eng/toolchain.json` (C-0009 section 2); the toolchain check fails when a job runs on another macOS image than the pinned one, and when it cannot read a job's runner in the spellings that [repository-checks.md](../../docs/design/repository-checks.md) section 5 lists.
- **Every failure in one run.** Each step after the setup runs even when an earlier step failed.
- **Telemetry.** The workflow sets the opt-out variables of the .NET CLI, Microsoft.Testing.Platform and Avalonia's build statistics, so CI runs send none.
- **Permissions.** The workflow can only read the repository, and the checkout keeps no credentials. lychee uses the workflow's token for links to github.com.
- **The ios job.** It runs for every pull request, so its result on the last commit is there before a merge, as C-0011 section 3 requires, and for every push to `main`, which catches two pull requests that pass alone and break together, and commits made directly on `main`. A newer push cancels its earlier run for the same pull request; each push to `main` gets a run of its own. A push to another branch without a pull request is not built for iOS.
- **The runtime job.** It runs the harness of `tests/runtime` on our own Win32 test programs under the Wine and FEX forks (C-0011 sections 1 and 4). Its caches are keyed as C-0011 section 4 says, and each fork build is saved right after it is built, so that a failing harness, a timeout or a cancelled run keeps it. A newer push to the same pull request waits for a running job instead of cancelling it, so that a cold build of Wine is never thrown away halfway, and the job stops after 90 minutes (D14).
- **Caches.** GitHub keeps 10 GB of caches for the repository. Only a push to `main` saves NuGet's packages, which every branch restores; a cache that a pull request saves is visible only to that pull request ([forks.md](../../docs/design/forks.md) section 8).
- **Still to come.** M8.3 adds the compatibility data step to `checks`, and M9.1 adds `release`.

To add or update an action, confirm its license and register it under C-0003 first, then map it in `eng/license-map.json` and pin the new release's commit hash. [solution-and-build.md](../../docs/design/solution-and-build.md) describes the build, and [repository-checks.md](../../docs/design/repository-checks.md) every check and step.
